中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架

经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听

briefs.speaker: Rashad Robinson
briefs.speaker_context: President of Color of Change, discussing his book 'From Presence to Power' and the difference between performative activism and actual political power
briefs.current_title: 拉沙德·罗宾逊：从“在场”到“权力”，行动主义如何避免自欺欺人？
current_title_lines: 行动主义如何避免自欺欺人？

subtitles.zh: 我们生活在一个点赞、分享、粉丝的时代，所以改变一个标题，常常被误认为真的改变了一套规则。
subtitles.en: Well, we live in this age of likes shares followers and so the kind of changing a headline get a mistaken for actually changing a set of rules.

subtitles.zh: 这就是“在场”和“权力”的区别。有时候，人们知道某个问题，这种意识会让我们很兴奋。
subtitles.en: That's the difference between presence and power and I think sometimes we can get really excited by the awareness that people sort of know about the issue.

subtitles.zh: 他们可能关心。我们甚至看到民调显示大多数美国人想要合理的枪支改革，但真正实现目标的权力，并不在于民调、意识或头条新闻。
subtitles.en: They may care. We may even see polling numbers that say you know the majority of Americans want sensible gun reform but the power to actually get there is not about the polling or the awareness or the headlines.

subtitles.zh: 它关乎你如何建立杠杆，如何改变激励结构，如何积聚足够的能量，从而推动那些原本不会发生的事情发生。
subtitles.en: It is about sort of all the ways in which you build leverage all the ways in which you change incentive structures all the ways in which you build enough energy so that you can force something happen that would not otherwise happen.

subtitles.zh: 我深有感触，这观点很好。作为报道过许多抗议活动的人，我总说：好吧，但你打算怎么做？
subtitles.en: I felt this point so deeply and I think it's such a good point because as someone who's covered so many protests the thing I always say is okay but how are you going to do that?

subtitles.zh: 你真正站出来喊口号，把Instagram头像换成一种颜色，这并不能解决问题。但我想知道，这是否可能产生反效果，因为那些可能不同意你的人……
subtitles.en: What are your actually standing out yelling changing your Instagram to a color is not going to do it but I'm wondering if it can almost even have the opposite effect because people who may disagree with you.

subtitles.zh: 或者那些同意你的人觉得你被过度代表了，也许问题已经解决了。看，我到处都看到这种情况，然后他们就不采取必要的行动了。
subtitles.en: Or people who may agree with you feel like you're overrepresented and maybe it's solved. Look I see it everywhere and then they don't take the action they need to.

subtitles.zh: 百分之百。当我们把“在场”当作“权力”时，你会以为有些事情已经发生了，但实际上并没有。
subtitles.en: 100% you know when we stake presence for power you could think something has happened that hasn't actually happened.

subtitles.zh: 比如有了黑人总统，就意味着后种族时代来了，所以人们认为所有工作都结束了。
subtitles.en: The black president meaning that your post-racial right so folks think all the work is over.

subtitles.zh: 你知道，关于抗议的一点是，它有时已经变成了精心编排的表演。
subtitles.en: You know the thing about protest as well is that someone that have just become choreography.

subtitles.zh: 人们在特定时间出现在特定地点，一天结束，一切清理干净，媒体周期继续。
subtitles.en: Folks show up to a certain place at a certain time by the end of the day everything's cleaned up the media cycle goes on.

subtitles.zh: 没有人担心会让那些站出来的人群失望。
subtitles.en: And no one is nervous about disappointing the communities that showed up.

briefs.speaker: Rashad Robinson
briefs.speaker_context: President of Color of Change, discussing his book 'From Presence to Power' and the difference between performative activism and actual political power
briefs.current_title: 拉沙德·罗宾逊：为什么我们一直在输？——行动主义需要新策略

subtitles.zh: 所以我们必须换一种思路，因为让我们陷入困境的策略，面对诸多挑战的方式，不会成为让我们脱困的答案。
subtitles.en: And so we do have to think differently because the strategies that sort of got us into this mess the sort of ways in which we are facing so many challenges they're not going to be the same challenges that get us out.

subtitles.zh: 我想对那些此刻站出来抗议、以不同方式发声的人说，他们常常问：为什么我们一直在输？
subtitles.en: And I think for those that have been showing up in this moment protesting raising their voices in different ways they're asking a lot of times of like why are we losing?

subtitles.zh: 为什么我们没有赢得更多？答案是问责吗？
subtitles.en: Why haven't we won more things? And the answer accountability?

subtitles.zh: 答案是，我们一直在用错误的策略。我们没有清晰分析该把斗争引向何处。
subtitles.en: Well the answer is that we've just been using the wrong strategies. The answer is that we haven't had a clear analysis around where we take the fights to.

subtitles.zh: 所以我认为，失败并认识到自己正在失败，是通往胜利的第一步。
subtitles.en: And so I think that losing and recognizing that you're losing is like the first step on the way to winning.

subtitles.zh: 因为我认为右翼做得非常有效的一件事是，他们改变了政治。
subtitles.en: Because I think one thing that the right wing has done really effective is they've changed politics.

subtitles.zh: 他们让每个人都有角色。所以人们戴着红帽子出现在世界上，如果你走进……
subtitles.en: They've made it so that everyone has a role. So people wear their red caps out in the world if you go into...

subtitles.zh: 一种有形的身份认同。
subtitles.en: A tangible identity.

subtitles.zh: 是的，他们走进健身房，改变着保守派媒体的挑战。
subtitles.en: Yeah they go into a gym they're changing the challenge of conservative media.

subtitles.zh: 他们做各种事情来塑造自己生活的环境。
subtitles.en: They're doing all sorts of things to shape the environment that they live in.

subtitles.zh: 很多时候，相信社会变革和进步的人们几乎是在低声细语地表达信念，或者只是出现在城里最舒适的地方参加抗议。
subtitles.en: And a lot of times for folks who believe in social change and progress are almost whispering their beliefs or maybe just showing up to a protest in the most comfortable part of town.

subtitles.zh: 在指定的日子，三小时后结束，大家回家，但其余时间他们并没有在世界上展现自己的能量。
subtitles.en: You know on the designated day where it gets wrapped up after three hours and everyone goes home but then the rest of their time they're not wearing their energy out in the world.

subtitles.zh: 因此，有时我们看起来几乎对自己的信念感到尴尬。
subtitles.en: And so as a result we can sometimes look like we're almost embarrassed by what we believe.

briefs.speaker: Rashad Robinson
briefs.speaker_context: President of Color of Change, discussing his book 'From Presence to Power' and the difference between performative activism and actual political power
briefs.current_title: 拉沙德·罗宾逊：与扎克伯格交锋，我学到了“对话”与“谈判”的区别

subtitles.zh: 你如何看待这种动态：你代表有真实不满、想要真正改变的人们，与那些已经达到一定地位、却不太考虑这些的人打交道？
subtitles.en: How did you think about the dynamic that you had and representing people who had real grievances and wanted real change with folks who'd really reached the session on where they hadn't been thinking about that very much?

subtitles.zh: 我在书中讲了很多这样的故事，因为我认为让人们了解幕后发生的事情非常重要。这些教训包括走进Facebook，试图推动马克·扎克伯格和谢丽尔·桑德伯格做出改变。
subtitles.en: So I tell a lot of stories in the book about this because I think it's really important to unlock for folks what happens behind the scenes because some of these lessons of going in and trying to push Mark Zuckerberg and Sheryl Sandberg at F

subtitles.zh: 你所做的，以及获得改变，实际上类似于参加学校董事会会议或当地图书馆董事会会议等。
subtitles.en: What you were doing is yes and getting and getting change is actually similar to like going into your school board meeting or going into your local library board or whatever.

subtitles.zh: 在这些来回交锋中，我学到的一件事是……
subtitles.en: And you know one of the things I learned in those back and forth.

subtitles.zh: 首先，我的第一次会议，我们终于建立了足够的杠杆去与马克和谢丽尔会面，此前媒体上有很多来回，他们还雇了公关公司攻击我和我的组织。
subtitles.en: Well first of all my first meeting where we finally built up enough leverage to go and meet with Mark and Sheryl after there was a lot of back and forth in the media and they had hired a PR firm to attack me in the organization.

subtitles.zh: 我到了门洛帕克，他们想让我签保密协议，我说不签，于是他们给了我一个背后写着NDA的大牌子，我必须戴着它在园区里走动。
subtitles.en: I get to Menlo Park and they want me to sign an NDA and I was like not signing an NDA so they give me a big back to says NDA on it that I have to wear around the campus.

subtitles.zh: 但因为我没有签那份保密协议，我才能讲述真实发生的故事。我学到的一件事是“对话”和“谈判”之间的区别。
subtitles.en: But because I didn't sign that NDA I'm actually tell real stories about what happened and one of the things I learned was the difference between being in a dialogue and negotiating.

subtitles.zh: 你的对手想让你停留在对话中。他们想说：我们正在和那个团体谈，我们听到了那些活动人士的声音。
subtitles.en: Your opponents want to keep you in a dialogue. They want to say we're talking to that group. We've heard those clive and activists.

subtitles.zh: 我们听到了对此不满的女性，我们在倾听，我们真的很关心。
subtitles.en: We've heard the women that are upset about this and we're listening to them and we're really concerned.

subtitles.zh: 当你处于谈判中时，你有杠杆，你有能力真正推动事情。但知道是仅仅进行一场感觉良好的对话，还是拥有真正做出有意义改变的能力，这就是“在场”和“权力”的区别。
subtitles.en: When you have it when you're in negotiation you have leverage. You have the ability to actually move something but knowing the difference between whether just in a conversation that feels good and whether or not you have the ability to actu

subtitles.zh: 很多时候，我们被激励着想要进入那个房间，想要感觉自己的声音被听到，担忧被放大，但这些并不等同于真正推动事情前进。
subtitles.en: And far too often we can be incentivized to want to be in the room. We want to be incentivized to feel like we've been shouted out or our concerns have been amplified but those are not the same as actually moving things along.

briefs.current_title: 拉沙德·罗宾逊：从同性婚姻到社会运动，如何用“信念文化”赢得人心？
current_title_lines: 从同性婚姻到社会运动
如何用“信念文化”赢得人心？

subtitles.zh: 我常听到“教育你不是我的责任”，这完全合理，但也可能适得其反。
subtitles.en: I hear a lot it's not on me to educate you and that's completely fair but it also might be counterproductive.

subtitles.zh: 我写了很多关于这个的内容，因为2005年到2011年间，我负责一些项目，在好莱坞和当地社区做了很多工作，我讲了一个以“信念文化”为中心的故事。
subtitles.en: I write a lot about this because between 2005 and 2011 I was ahead of programs that glad and did a lot of work in Hollywood and in local communities and I tell a story centered on the culture of belief.

subtitles.zh: 记得2006年，我去过阿拉巴马州和得克萨斯州深红地区，培训情侣们讲述他们的故事，并开始把结婚启事登在报纸上。
subtitles.en: Back 2006 I remember going to places like Alabama and deep red parts of Texas and training couples to both tell their stories but also start putting their wedding announcements in the newspaper

subtitles.zh: 早在婚姻平等成为议题之前，我们就推动报纸接受同性结婚启事。因为当时的研究告诉我们，一旦人们认识同性恋伴侣，知道他们就在身边，他们就不再是“另类”。
subtitles.en: long before marriage equality was a thing and forcing advocating to have newspapers except those same sex wedding announcements right because what we knew from the research at the time is that more people once they knew gay and lesbian coup

subtitles.zh: 是的，但我们也看到人们不谈论自己的生活，他们可能出柜了，但之后并没有与生活中的异性恋者进行对话，所以人们没有被“投入”其中。

- A candidate is usable only if one emotion pole is unmistakable and emotion_tension is at least 8/10.
- The six permitted poles are: unexpected reversal, pleasant surprise, strong doubt, finally-someone-said-it candor, verified words-versus-actions contrast, and fact-based pride in a Chinese comparative advantage.
- Do not split the emotion across several mild ideas. Pick one pole and push it to the factual limit.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

Title and display rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Use exactly three non-empty title lines, each a punchy cover block. Ideal lengths: 3-10, 4-12, 5-14 Chinese characters.
- Full title should be short and sharp, ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- Keep only one core conflict. Do not pack background, claim, caveat, and conclusion into one line.
- Highlights must be exact substrings of joined title_lines and emphasize the actor, number, reversal, China advantage, or tension.
- Do not use flat endings such as 回报路径在哪、回报存疑、前景如何、未来如何、有待观察、仍不明朗、面临挑战、带来机遇、释放信号、关键分叉在哪、有望扩大. Turn the caveat into a concrete unresolved action or contradiction.
- Every line must be a complete Chinese phrase. Do not leave a transitive tension verb such as 逼急、逼到、迫使 or 倒逼 without its subject or object.
- Do not use source badges, emojis, markdown, quotation marks, hashtags, or numbering.
- Title fields must not contain 资产管理、投资、股票、基金、理财、保险、投顾、荐股、买入、卖出.
- Never use 经济危机、金融危机、债务危机、危机、崩盘、崩溃、完了、没救、惨了.
- Do not mention sensitive geopolitical or military topics.

KC comment rules:
- comment starts with KC评论： and adds context, consequence, or the next fact to watch in 16-34 Chinese characters. Do not repeat the title.
- subtitle_comments contains one item for every input subtitle index, grounded in that exact subtitle rather than a generic clip slogan.
- Each subtitle comment starts with KC评论： and is ideally 10-24 Chinese characters after the prefix, with a complete ending.
- Adjacent subtitle comments must vary between evidence, implication, tension, consequence, and context.
- All highlight strings must be exact substrings of their corresponding title/comment.

briefs.speaker: Randall Williams
briefs.speaker_context: Bloomberg News US Sports reporter, discussing the record-breaking Lakers sale and Knicks-Rangers split
briefs.current_title: 湖人队天价易主：鲍勃·艾格与乔什·库什纳72小时闪电交易
current_title_lines: 彭博体育记者兰德尔·威廉姆斯

subtitles.zh: 没错，正如你所说，鲍勃·艾格和乔什·库什纳原本在考虑拉斯维加斯的NBA扩军球队。
subtitles.en: Sure. So as you said, Bob Eiger and Josh Kushner were looking at the NBA expansion team in Las Vegas.

subtitles.zh: 艾格告诉我，当时价格越抬越高。后来有内部消息人士或中间人建议他们：不如去看看湖人队。
subtitles.en: And then the price was getting high as what Eiger told me. And at some point, a little birdie or an intermediary suggested or told Bob Eiger and Josh Kushner, hey, you should go look at the Lakers.

subtitles.zh: 果然，那大概是在周六或周日。大约72小时，也许90小时后，他们就达成了交易。
subtitles.en: And sure enough that had to be on Saturday or Sunday. And some 72 hours later, maybe 90 hours later, they had to deal.

subtitles.zh: 他们原本在拉斯维加斯，打算从零开始组建球队。兰德尔，发生了什么？我认为沃尔玛家族，也就是沃尔顿家族参与其中。
subtitles.en: They were looking in Vegas. They were going to start a team from scratch, Randall. What happened? I really think that there's a Walmart family involved, or a Walton family involved.

subtitles.zh: 拉斯维加斯还有其他几个集团参与，包括金骑士队老板戈福利，还有马克·拉扎里及其团队，即拉斯维加斯杰克队。
subtitles.en: And there's a couple of other groups involved in Las Vegas, including GoFoli, who's the owner of the Golden Knights. And then you have Mark Lazarie and the group known as the Las Vegas Jacks.

subtitles.zh: 这么多集团参与，竞争自然会推高价格。乔什·库什纳和鲍勃·艾格原本是热门人选。
subtitles.en: When you have that many groups involved, naturally, that competition is going to drive the price high. Now, Josh Kushner and Bob Eiger were considered favorites.

subtitles.zh: 不过，如果他们都觉得价格太高，我只能猜测，成交价可能超过100亿美元。
subtitles.en: However, if they say it's high, I can only imagine that I would guesstimate that it's over $10 billion.

briefs.speaker: Randall Williams
briefs.speaker_context: Bloomberg News US Sports reporter, discussing the record-breaking Lakers sale and Knicks-Rangers split
briefs.current_title: 尼克斯与游骑兵分拆：麦迪逊广场花园体育公司价值重估
current_title_lines: 彭博体育记者兰德尔·威廉姆斯
价值重估或引巨头入股

subtitles.zh: 兰德尔和我一起参加了纽约尼克斯队的游行，我们共同经历了那件事。
subtitles.en: Randall and I, we were at the New York Knicks Parade, so we did that together.

subtitles.zh: 我们在那里玩得很开心。但现在，尼克斯队与纽约游骑兵队分拆的计划越来越近，到底怎么回事？能成吗？
subtitles.en: We had a great time out there. But now all this, the Knicks moving closer to this New York Ranger spin-off, I mean, what's going on? Is this going through?

subtitles.zh: 我觉得能成。尼克斯队，或者说麦迪逊广场花园体育公司，正计划将游骑兵队的业务从尼克斯队的业务中分离出来。
subtitles.en: I think so. I think the Knicks or Madison Square Garden Sports Corporation is targeting separating the Rangers business from the Knicks business.

subtitles.zh: 这意味着麦迪逊广场花园体育公司将更名为麦迪逊广场花园尼克斯公司，而游骑兵队将成为独立的业务。
subtitles.en: And so what this will mean is that Madison Square Garden Sports Corporation will become the Madison Square Garden Knicks Corporation, and then there will be a separate Rangers business.

subtitles.zh: 预计这将释放价值，厘清尼克斯业务与游骑兵业务之间的差异。
subtitles.en: What's expected to happen is this is going to extract value. This is going to figure out the difference between the Knicks business and the Rangers business.

subtitles.zh: 詹姆斯·多兰表示，他没有出售任何一支球队的计划。
subtitles.en: And James Dolan has said that he has no plans of selling either team.

subtitles.zh: 但一旦这些球队的价值显现，谁能说他不能以20%的股份获得20亿美元，甚至15%的股份呢？
subtitles.en: But once you see the value of those teams, who's to say he couldn't get $2 billion for 20% of the team, or maybe even 15% of the team?

briefs.speaker: Randall Williams
briefs.speaker_context: Bloomberg News US Sports reporter, discussing the record-breaking Lakers sale and Knicks-Rangers split
briefs.current_title: AI时代体育资产为何坚挺？兰德尔：现场体验无可替代
current_title_lines: 彭博体育记者兰德尔·威廉姆斯
AI时代体育资产为何坚挺

subtitles.zh: 有趣的是，金融时报也有一篇报道。我们之前和ABC新闻前负责人大卫·韦斯顿在节目中讨论过。
subtitles.en: You know what's interesting. I think the FT had a piece too. And we talked about this on air with David Weston, of course, formerly head of ABC News.

subtitles.zh: 他认识鲍勃·艾格。我们正在讨论这个观点，兰德尔，我很好奇你们听到了什么。
subtitles.en: He knows Bob Iger. But we were talking about this idea at Randall, and I'm curious what you guys are hearing.

subtitles.zh: 人们对体育球队的兴趣似乎对人工智能具有韧性。
subtitles.en: That the interest in sports teams kind of resilient to AI, artificial intelligence.

subtitles.zh: 在我们这个充满不确定性的世界里，我觉得很多领域都会受到影响，但体育可能不会。
subtitles.en: As we think about it in a world where we don't know, I feel like a lot's going to be impacted. Sports, maybe not so much.

subtitles.zh: 现场体育，先生。是的，我怀疑它不会。我目前持怀疑态度。
subtitles.en: Live sports, sir. Yeah, I doubt it. I doubt it right now.

subtitles.zh: 我认为AI会增强体育体验。想象一下走进一座新球馆。
subtitles.en: I think that AI will enhance sports experiences. You think about walking into a new arena.

subtitles.zh: 如果你是资深季票持有者，你的体验是否已经个性化？球馆或你的应用会说：欢迎回来，卡罗尔？
subtitles.en: If you're a seasoned ticket holder, is your experience now customized? Do the arena or does your app say welcome back, Carol?

subtitles.zh: 我们很高兴为您提供上次吃过的烤鸡。这种定制化体验正是我所期待的。
subtitles.en: We'd love to have you eat the barbecue chicken you had last time. Sort of those customized experiences is what I expect.

subtitles.zh: 长期来看，如果有人能创建一个基于技术的联赛，比如机器人什么的，我认为那还很遥远，那是我看到的唯一威胁，但目前还看不到。
subtitles.en: Now, long term, if someone's able to create a technology based league, something with robots or something that I think is where far away from, that's the only threat that I see, but it's not in sight.

subtitles.zh: 那只是幻想。我得问问你，你还好吗？
subtitles.en: It's a fantasy. I got to ask you, are you okay?

Use the research guide as a hard boundary: unsupported surprise, dishonesty, holdings, public actions, and national comparisons are forbidden. Wording guard for all Chinese output:
- Do not use hard crisis/doom financial wording such as 经济危机、金融危机、债务危机、流动性危机、危机、崩盘、崩溃、完了、没救、惨了、萧条、衰退.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

Title and display rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Use exactly three non-empty title lines, each a punchy cover block. Ideal lengths: 3-10, 4-12, 5-14 Chinese characters.
- Full title should be short and sharp, ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- Keep only one core conflict. Do not pack background, claim, caveat, and conclusion into one line.
- Highlights must be exact substrings of joined title_lines and emphasize the actor, number, reversal, China advantage, or tension.
- Do not use flat endings such as 回报路径在哪、回报存疑、前景如何、未来如何、有待观察、仍不明朗、面临挑战、带来机遇、释放信号、关键分叉在哪、有望扩大. Turn the caveat into a concrete unresolved action or contradiction.
- Every line must be a complete Chinese phrase. Do not leave a transitive tension verb such as 逼急、逼到、迫使 or 倒逼 without its subject or object.
- Do not use source badges, emojis, markdown, quotation marks, hashtags, or numbering.
- Title fields must not contain 资产管理、投资、股票、基金、理财、保险、投顾、荐股、买入、卖出.
- Never use 经济危机、金融危机、债务危机、危机、崩盘、崩溃、完了、没救、惨了.
- Do not mention sensitive geopolitical or military topics.

KC comment rules:
- comment starts with KC评论： and adds context, consequence, or the next fact to watch in 16-34 Chinese characters. Do not repeat the title.
- subtitle_comments contains one item for every input subtitle index, grounded in that exact subtitle rather than a generic clip slogan.
- Each subtitle comment starts with KC评论： and is ideally 10-24 Chinese characters after the prefix, with a complete ending.
- Adjacent subtitle comments must vary between evidence, implication, tension, consequence, and context.
- All highlight strings must be exact substrings of their corresponding title/comment.

briefs.speaker_context: President of Color of Change, discussing his book 'From Presence to Power' and the difference between performative activism and actual political power
briefs.current_title: 拉沙德·罗宾逊：从“在场”到“权力”，行动主义如何避免自欺欺人？
current_title_lines: 行动主义如何避免自欺欺人？

subtitles.zh: 我们生活在一个点赞、分享、粉丝的时代，所以改变一个标题，常常被误认为真的改变了一套规则。
subtitles.en: Well, we live in this age of likes shares followers and so the kind of changing a headline get a mistaken for actually changing a set of rules.

subtitles.zh: 这就是“在场”和“权力”的区别。有时候，人们知道某个问题，这种意识会让我们很兴奋。
subtitles.en: That's the difference between presence and power and I think sometimes we can get really excited by the awareness that people sort of know about the issue.

subtitles.zh: 他们可能关心。我们甚至看到民调显示大多数美国人想要合理的枪支改革，但真正实现目标的权力，并不在于民调、意识或头条新闻。
subtitles.en: They may care. We may even see polling numbers that say you know the majority of Americans want sensible gun reform but the power to actually get there is not about the polling or the awareness or the headlines.

subtitles.zh: 它关乎你如何建立杠杆，如何改变激励结构，如何积聚足够的能量，从而推动那些原本不会发生的事情发生。
subtitles.en: It is about sort of all the ways in which you build leverage all the ways in which you change incentive structures all the ways in which you build enough energy so that you can force something happen that would not otherwise happen.

subtitles.zh: 我深有感触，这观点很好。作为报道过许多抗议活动的人，我总说：好吧，但你打算怎么做？
subtitles.en: I felt this point so deeply and I think it's such a good point because as someone who's covered so many protests the thing I always say is okay but how are you going to do that?

subtitles.zh: 你真正站出来喊口号，把Instagram头像换成一种颜色，这并不能解决问题。但我想知道，这是否可能产生反效果，因为那些可能不同意你的人……
subtitles.en: What are your actually standing out yelling changing your Instagram to a color is not going to do it but I'm wondering if it can almost even have the opposite effect because people who may disagree with you.

subtitles.zh: 或者那些同意你的人觉得你被过度代表了，也许问题已经解决了。看，我到处都看到这种情况，然后他们就不采取必要的行动了。
subtitles.en: Or people who may agree with you feel like you're overrepresented and maybe it's solved. Look I see it everywhere and then they don't take the action they need to.

subtitles.zh: 百分之百。当我们把“在场”当作“权力”时，你会以为有些事情已经发生了，但实际上并没有。
subtitles.en: 100% you know when we stake presence for power you could think something has happened that hasn't actually happened.

subtitles.zh: 比如有了黑人总统，就意味着后种族时代来了，所以人们认为所有工作都结束了。
subtitles.en: The black president meaning that your post-racial right so folks think all the work is over.

subtitles.zh: 你知道，关于抗议的一点是，它有时已经变成了精心编排的表演。
subtitles.en: You know the thing about protest as well is that someone that have just become choreography.

subtitles.zh: 人们在特定时间出现在特定地点，一天结束，一切清理干净，媒体周期继续。
subtitles.en: Folks show up to a certain place at a certain time by the end of the day everything's cleaned up the media cycle goes on.

subtitles.zh: 没有人担心会让那些站出来的人群失望。
subtitles.en: And no one is nervous about disappointing the communities that showed up.

briefs.current_title: 拉沙德·罗宾逊：为什么我们一直在输？——行动主义需要新策略

subtitles.zh: 所以我们必须换一种思路，因为让我们陷入困境的策略，面对诸多挑战的方式，不会成为让我们脱困的答案。
subtitles.en: And so we do have to think differently because the strategies that sort of got us into this mess the sort of ways in which we are facing so many challenges they're not going to be the same challenges that get us out.

subtitles.zh: 我想对那些此刻站出来抗议、以不同方式发声的人说，他们常常问：为什么我们一直在输？
subtitles.en: And I think for those that have been showing up in this moment protesting raising their voices in different ways they're asking a lot of times of like why are we losing?

subtitles.zh: 为什么我们没有赢得更多？答案是问责吗？
subtitles.en: Why haven't we won more things? And the answer accountability?

subtitles.zh: 答案是，我们一直在用错误的策略。我们没有清晰分析该把斗争引向何处。
subtitles.en: Well the answer is that we've just been using the wrong strategies. The answer is that we haven't had a clear analysis around where we take the fights to.

subtitles.zh: 所以我认为，失败并认识到自己正在失败，是通往胜利的第一步。
subtitles.en: And so I think that losing and recognizing that you're losing is like the first step on the way to winning.

subtitles.zh: 因为我认为右翼做得非常有效的一件事是，他们改变了政治。
subtitles.en: Because I think one thing that the right wing has done really effective is they've changed politics.

subtitles.zh: 他们让每个人都有角色。所以人们戴着红帽子出现在世界上，如果你走进……
subtitles.en: They've made it so that everyone has a role. So people wear their red caps out in the world if you go into...

subtitles.zh: 一种有形的身份认同。
subtitles.en: A tangible identity.

subtitles.zh: 是的，他们走进健身房，改变着保守派媒体的挑战。
subtitles.en: Yeah they go into a gym they're changing the challenge of conservative media.

subtitles.zh: 他们做各种事情来塑造自己生活的环境。
subtitles.en: They're doing all sorts of things to shape the environment that they live in.

subtitles.zh: 很多时候，相信社会变革和进步的人们几乎是在低声细语地表达信念，或者只是出现在城里最舒适的地方参加抗议。
subtitles.en: And a lot of times for folks who believe in social change and progress are almost whispering their beliefs or maybe just showing up to a protest in the most comfortable part of town.

subtitles.zh: 在指定的日子，三小时后结束，大家回家，但其余时间他们并没有在世界上展现自己的能量。
subtitles.en: You know on the designated day where it gets wrapped up after three hours and everyone goes home but then the rest of their time they're not wearing their energy out in the world.

subtitles.zh: 因此，有时我们看起来几乎对自己的信念感到尴尬。
subtitles.en: And so as a result we can sometimes look like we're almost embarrassed by what we believe.

subtitles.en: So I tell a lot of stories in the book about this because I think it's really important to unlock for folks what happens behind the scenes because some of these lessons of going in and trying to push Mark Zuckerberg and Sheryl Sandberg at F

subtitles.zh: 你所做的，以及获得改变，实际上类似于参加学校董事会会议或当地图书馆董事会会议等。
subtitles.en: What you were doing is yes and getting and getting change is actually similar to like going into your school board meeting or going into your local library board or whatever.

subtitles.zh: 在这些来回交锋中，我学到的一件事是……
subtitles.en: And you know one of the things I learned in those back and forth.

subtitles.zh: 首先，我的第一次会议，我们终于建立了足够的杠杆去与马克和谢丽尔会面，此前媒体上有很多来回，他们还雇了公关公司攻击我和我的组织。
subtitles.en: Well first of all my first meeting where we finally built up enough leverage to go and meet with Mark and Sheryl after there was a lot of back and forth in the media and they had hired a PR firm to attack me in the organization.

subtitles.zh: 我到了门洛帕克，他们想让我签保密协议，我说不签，于是他们给了我一个背后写着NDA的大牌子，我必须戴着它在园区里走动。
subtitles.en: I get to Menlo Park and they want me to sign an NDA and I was like not signing an NDA so they give me a big back to says NDA on it that I have to wear around the campus.

subtitles.zh: 但因为我没有签那份保密协议，我才能讲述真实发生的故事。我学到的一件事是“对话”和“谈判”之间的区别。
subtitles.en: But because I didn't sign that NDA I'm actually tell real stories about what happened and one of the things I learned was the difference between being in a dialogue and negotiating.

subtitles.zh: 你的对手想让你停留在对话中。他们想说：我们正在和那个团体谈，我们听到了那些活动人士的声音。
subtitles.en: Your opponents want to keep you in a dialogue. They want to say we're talking to that group. We've heard those clive and activists.

subtitles.zh: 我们听到了对此不满的女性，我们在倾听，我们真的很关心。
subtitles.en: We've heard the women that are upset about this and we're listening to them and we're really concerned.

subtitles.zh: 当你处于谈判中时，你有杠杆，你有能力真正推动事情。但知道是仅仅进行一场感觉良好的对话，还是拥有真正做出有意义改变的能力，这就是“在场”和“权力”的区别。
subtitles.en: When you have it when you're in negotiation you have leverage. You have the ability to actually move something but knowing the difference between whether just in a conversation that feels good and whether or not you have the ability to actu

subtitles.zh: 很多时候，我们被激励着想要进入那个房间，想要感觉自己的声音被听到，担忧被放大，但这些并不等同于真正推动事情前进。
subtitles.en: And far too often we can be incentivized to want to be in the room. We want to be incentivized to feel like we've been shouted out or our concerns have been amplified but those are not the same as actually moving things along.

briefs.current_title: 湖人队天价易主：鲍勃·艾格与乔什·库什纳72小时闪电交易
current_title_lines: 彭博体育记者兰德尔·威廉姆斯

subtitles.zh: 没错，正如你所说，鲍勃·艾格和乔什·库什纳原本在考虑拉斯维加斯的NBA扩军球队。
subtitles.en: Sure. So as you said, Bob Eiger and Josh Kushner were looking at the NBA expansion team in Las Vegas.

subtitles.zh: 艾格告诉我，当时价格越抬越高。后来有内部消息人士或中间人建议他们：不如去看看湖人队。
subtitles.en: And then the price was getting high as what Eiger told me. And at some point, a little birdie or an intermediary suggested or told Bob Eiger and Josh Kushner, hey, you should go look at the Lakers.

subtitles.zh: 果然，那大概是在周六或周日。大约72小时，也许90小时后，他们就达成了交易。
subtitles.en: And sure enough that had to be on Saturday or Sunday. And some 72 hours later, maybe 90 hours later, they had to deal.

subtitles.zh: 他们原本在拉斯维加斯，打算从零开始组建球队。兰德尔，发生了什么？我认为沃尔玛家族，也就是沃尔顿家族参与其中。
subtitles.en: They were looking in Vegas. They were going to start a team from scratch, Randall. What happened? I really think that there's a Walmart family involved, or a Walton family involved.

subtitles.zh: 拉斯维加斯还有其他几个集团参与，包括金骑士队老板戈福利，还有马克·拉扎里及其团队，即拉斯维加斯杰克队。
subtitles.en: And there's a couple of other groups involved in Las Vegas, including GoFoli, who's the owner of the Golden Knights. And then you have Mark Lazarie and the group known as the Las Vegas Jacks.

subtitles.zh: 这么多集团参与，竞争自然会推高价格。乔什·库什纳和鲍勃·艾格原本是热门人选。
subtitles.en: When you have that many groups involved, naturally, that competition is going to drive the price high. Now, Josh Kushner and Bob Eiger were considered favorites.

subtitles.zh: 不过，如果他们都觉得价格太高，我只能猜测，成交价可能超过100亿美元。
subtitles.en: However, if they say it's high, I can only imagine that I would guesstimate that it's over $10 billion.

subtitles.zh: 兰德尔和我一起参加了纽约尼克斯队的游行，我们共同经历了那件事。
subtitles.en: Randall and I, we were at the New York Knicks Parade, so we did that together.

subtitles.zh: 我们在那里玩得很开心。但现在，尼克斯队与纽约游骑兵队分拆的计划越来越近，到底怎么回事？能成吗？
subtitles.en: We had a great time out there. But now all this, the Knicks moving closer to this New York Ranger spin-off, I mean, what's going on? Is this going through?

subtitles.zh: 我觉得能成。尼克斯队，或者说麦迪逊广场花园体育公司，正计划将游骑兵队的业务从尼克斯队的业务中分离出来。
subtitles.en: I think so. I think the Knicks or Madison Square Garden Sports Corporation is targeting separating the Rangers business from the Knicks business.

subtitles.zh: 这意味着麦迪逊广场花园体育公司将更名为麦迪逊广场花园尼克斯公司，而游骑兵队将成为独立的业务。
subtitles.en: And so what this will mean is that Madison Square Garden Sports Corporation will become the Madison Square Garden Knicks Corporation, and then there will be a separate Rangers business.

subtitles.zh: 预计这将释放价值，厘清尼克斯业务与游骑兵业务之间的差异。
subtitles.en: What's expected to happen is this is going to extract value. This is going to figure out the difference between the Knicks business and the Rangers business.

subtitles.zh: 詹姆斯·多兰表示，他没有出售任何一支球队的计划。
subtitles.en: And James Dolan has said that he has no plans of selling either team.

subtitles.zh: 但一旦这些球队的价值显现，谁能说他不能以20%的股份获得20亿美元，甚至15%的股份呢？
subtitles.en: But once you see the value of those teams, who's to say he couldn't get $2 billion for 20% of the team, or maybe even 15% of the team?
